data.claim: Will America or Israel bomb Iran again before Thanksgiving?

current.title: US and Israel strikes on Iran

data.resolution_source: Official statements by the US Department of Defense, US Central Command or the White House, or by the Israel Defense Forces or the Israeli Prime Minister's Office; or reporting by at least two of Reuters, the Associated Press and Axios.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, between 2026-10-20T09:00Z and 2026-11-25T23:59Z, US or Israeli forces carry out at least one air, missile or drone strike on a target on Iranian territory: the mainland, Iranian-held islands, or ships moored at an Iranian port or base. A strike launched at such a target counts whether or not Iranian defences intercept it. The strike must be acknowledged by one of the named governments or reported as a US or Israeli strike by at least two of the named outlets, in their own reporting or citing US or Israeli officials; Iranian accusations alone do not count, nor do reports the outlets have retracted by the end of 2026-11-28. Not counted: blockade enforcement or other action against vessels at sea, including inside Iran's territorial waters; interception of Iranian missiles, drones or boats; strikes on Iranian-backed groups or Iranian assets outside Iran; cyberattacks; and sabotage or killings inside Iran that neither government acknowledges and the named outlets do not report as a US or Israeli strike. A strike before Nov. 3 counts the same as one after it. Acknowledgements and reports published up to the end of 2026-11-28 count for strikes within the window. If no qualifying strike in the window has been acknowledged or reported by the end of 2026-11-28, the question resolves No.

data.claim: Will diesel cost Americans more in two weeks than now?
data.resolution_source: US Energy Information Administration, Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update, weekly U.S. on-highway diesel fuel price (all types), https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the US average on-highway diesel price for the week of Nov. 9, 2026, as first published by the EIA, is above $6.352 a gallon, the reading for Oct. 26, 2026 published on Oct. 27. No if it is $6.352 or lower. If the EIA has not published the Nov. 9 reading by Nov. 10, 2026, the question is void.

data.claim: Will America keep its Ebola ban on visitors from Uganda?
data.resolution_source: CDC's order page for the Ebola entry suspension (cdc.gov/port-health/legal-authorities/evdorder.html), the Federal Register, or an official CDC, HHS or DHS statement
data.resolution_rule: The moment that counts is 5:00 pm US Eastern time on Nov. 10, 2026, when the current order expires. Yes if a US federal order in force at that moment bars entry to foreign nationals because they were in Uganda, or any part of it, within a set period before arrival. The order can be a CDC renewal, an amendment, a successor order or a presidential proclamation, issued before or on Nov. 10 or later with effect from that moment, and it counts whether or not Congo and South Sudan are also listed. It must be shown by the source by Nov. 17, 2026. No if no such order is in force at that moment: the order lapsed or ended, or was amended so that having been in Uganda no longer by itself bars a foreign national from entry. Changes after that moment do not alter the answer. Measures that apply only to US citizens or permanent residents, such as routing through designated airports or extra screening, do not count as yes. If by Nov. 17, 2026 the source shows no order in force at that moment, the answer is no.

data.claim: Will Apple keep selling the iPhone Duo through Black Friday?
data.resolution_source: Apple's US online store and Apple Newsroom statements, the US Consumer Product Safety Commission recalls list, and Reuters or Bloomberg reporting on any iPhone Duo sales halt or recall.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, from the cutoff through the end of Nov. 27, 2026, US Pacific time, Apple neither (a) stops selling the iPhone Duo in the US because of its inner-display or hinge problem, meaning Apple stops taking new US orders for every Duo configuration and Apple, a regulator, Reuters or Bloomberg attributes the pause to the defect, nor (b) announces, or is ordered by a regulator in any country to carry out, a recall of the iPhone Duo, meaning return, repair or replacement offered for units that have not failed. A pause in that window counts even if sales later resume or a revised Duo replaces the original; a pause announced for a date after Nov. 27 does not. These do not count as stopping sales: sold-out notices, long delivery dates, store stock-outs, the current free replacement of failed units, an extended warranty for display failures, or a switch to a revised Duo with no pause in taking orders. Only a halt or recall reported by the end of Nov. 30, 2026 counts; if none is reported by then, the answer is yes.

data.claim: Will Beijing take new steps to prop up stocks by early December?
data.resolution_source: Official announcements on the websites of the State Council, People's Bank of China, China Securities Regulatory Commission, National Financial Regulatory Administration, Ministry of Finance, the Shanghai, Shenzhen or Beijing stock exchanges, Central Huijin or another named state investor; or Reuters or Bloomberg reports of such an official announcement.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, between 2026-10-28 09:00 UTC and 2026-12-08 23:59 Beijing time, a source body publicly announces a concrete new step to support mainland share prices, as published by it or reported by Reuters or Bloomberg by 2026-12-09 23:59 Beijing time. Counts: (a) Central Huijin or another named state investor says on the record it has bought or will buy mainland shares or stock funds; (b) the central bank creates, enlarges or extends a lending facility for share purchases or buybacks; (c) a cut to stamp duty or other taxes or fees on share trading; (d) looser margin-lending rules, such as a minimum margin deposit below the 100% set in January 2026; (e) a formal slowing or pause of new listings, or new limits on share sales by major shareholders; (f) a rule raising how much insurers or pension funds may or must hold in shares; (g) a new state-backed fund whose stated purpose is buying listed shares. Does not count: general pledges or meeting readouts without a concrete measure; unnamed-source reports of informal guidance; steps announced before the window, including the mid-October guidance, the outbound investment rules effective Dec. 1 and the 60 billion yuan National AI Industry Investment Fund; economy-wide interest-rate or reserve-requirement cuts; companies buying back their own shares; curbs that tighten trading. A step counts once announced, even if later delayed or reversed. Otherwise No.

data.claim: Will Korea's central bank hold off on raising rates in November?
data.resolution_source: Bank of Korea monetary policy decision announcement for its Monetary Policy Board meeting scheduled for Nov. 26, 2026 (bok.or.kr press release, published the same day), and any Bank of Korea announcement of a base rate change between Oct. 23 and Nov. 26, 2026.
data.resolution_rule: No if the Bank of Korea announces any rise in its base rate between Oct. 23 and Nov. 26, 2026, whether at its November meeting or at an unscheduled meeting. Otherwise Yes once the November decision is announced, whether it holds or cuts. The rate as announced on the decision day counts; later reversals do not change the result. If no November meeting has been held by Nov. 26, 2026 because it was moved later or called off, and no rise was announced in the window, the question is void.

data.claim: Will Germany's imported chips and electronic parts get dearer even faster?
data.resolution_source: Destatis (Federal Statistical Office) press release on import prices for September 2026 (Außenhandelspreise / Importpreise im September 2026), with GENESIS-Online table 61411-0006, product GP09-261 (electronic components), as a fallback.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the first-published year-on-year change in the German import price index for electronic components (elektronische Bauelemente) for September 2026 is greater than +16.1%, the figure Destatis published for August 2026. No if it is +16.1% or lower. If the press release does not give the electronic-components figure, compute it from the GENESIS index values for GP09-261 as first published on or before 2026-10-30, September 2026 against September 2025, rounded to one decimal. Later revisions are ignored. Void if by 2026-10-30 Destatis has not published September 2026 import prices, or neither the press release nor GENESIS gives the figure.

data.claim: Will America keep Nigeria and Kenya off its Ebola travel ban?
data.resolution_source: CDC Port Health legal authorities page for the order suspending entry from countries where Ebola exists (cdc.gov/port-health/legal-authorities/evdorder.html), the CDC's Oct. 22, 2026 boarding declaration order, and any related Federal Register notices
data.resolution_rule: No if any CDC Ebola order signed from Oct. 27 to Nov. 12, 2026 bars entry to the US, or boarding of a US-bound flight, for presence in Nigeria or Kenya in the prior 21 days. This covers adding either country to the entry suspension order (when renewed, amended or let lapse at its Nov. 10 expiry), to the Oct. 22 boarding declaration order, or to any new or replacement order. It counts even if it takes effect after Nov. 12 or is withdrawn later. Yes otherwise. This includes the case where the CDC page and the Federal Register, as published by Nov. 17, 2026, show no such order. State Department advisory levels, CDC travel health notices, entry limits based on nationality and not tied to Ebola, and screening or airport routing that does not bar entry or boarding do not count.

data.claim: Will more German factories be short of parts in October?
data.resolution_source: Ifo Institute monthly release on material shortages in German manufacturing (ifo.de), covering its October 2026 survey, or German press reports of that release.
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the share of manufacturing firms reporting shortages of materials or intermediate products in Ifo's October 2026 survey, as first published by Ifo, is higher than the September 2026 share of 14.6% (or higher than the September figure stated in the October release, if Ifo revises it). No if it is equal or lower. Later revisions to the October figure do not count. Sector figures do not count; only the all-manufacturing share. Where press reports differ from Ifo, Ifo's figure counts. Void if Ifo has not published the October figure by 19 November 2026.

data.claim: Will Anthropic's shares start trading before Thanksgiving?
data.resolution_source: Nasdaq trading records and Anthropic's pricing announcement or final prospectus (SEC Rule 424(b) filing), as reported by Reuters, Bloomberg, AP or CNBC
data.resolution_rule: Yes if Anthropic's common stock (expected ticker ANT, though a different ticker or share class still counts) begins regular trading on the Nasdaq, or on any other U.S. national securities exchange, on or before Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026 (U.S. Eastern time). The date of the first regular trading session decides; a later halt, delisting or withdrawal does not undo it. Pricing the offering does not count unless regular trading also starts by then. When-issued, pre-IPO, private secondary or tokenized trading does not count. No if regular trading has not begun by the end of Nov. 25, 2026, for any reason, including a postponement or withdrawal of the offering; a postponement still counts as Yes if trading nonetheless begins by Nov. 25. Reports published through Nov. 28, 2026 count toward showing when trading began; if none of the named outlets or Nasdaq records show trading beginning by Nov. 25 by then, the answer is No. The offering's size, price, valuation and first-day performance do not affect resolution.

data.claim: Will an iPhone Duo ordered on Black Friday still miss Christmas?
data.resolution_source: Apple's US online store (apple.com) estimated delivery dates for new iPhone Duo orders, as shown on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. Evidence is a capture of the store page showing those estimates (for example the Internet Archive) or a report by MacRumors, 9to5Mac, AppleInsider or Bloomberg describing them, published by Nov. 30, 2026.
data.resolution_rule: No if, at any time on Nov. 27, 2026 (US Pacific time), Apple's US online store shows an estimated home-delivery date on or before Dec. 25, 2026 for any iPhone Duo configuration (any storage size, colour, unlocked or carrier model). Otherwise Yes if every configuration it offers shows Dec. 26, 2026 or later, or cannot be ordered online (sold out, unavailable or sales halted), including when no configuration can be ordered at all. Where a date range is shown, its earliest date counts; a ship date counts as the delivery date, and a wait such as '4-5 weeks' is counted from Nov. 27. Use the default US estimate shown without a ZIP code, or the estimate for ZIP 10001 if a ZIP is required. Not counted: in-store pickup, walk-in stock, carriers' and other retailers' own channels, and changes to existing orders. A report that gives the store's estimate without naming configurations is read as covering all of them. If no capture or report published by Nov. 30 shows the estimates on Nov. 27, the latest one from Nov. 26 decides, else the earliest from Nov. 28; if there is none from those three days, the answer is No.

data.claim: Will Apple go two more weeks without promising free Duo screen repairs?
data.resolution_source: Apple's service programs page (support.apple.com/service-programs) and Apple Newsroom; Apple statements and executive remarks, including the Nov. 2, 2026 earnings call, as reported by Reuters, Bloomberg, MacRumors, AppleInsider or 9to5Mac.
data.resolution_rule: Window: Oct. 26 through Nov. 9, 2026, US Pacific time. Yes if in that window Apple makes no public commitment to repair or replace, at no charge, the iPhone Duo's inner display or hinge for affected owners generally in at least one country. No if in the window Apple publishes a service program under which Duo inner displays or hinges are repaired or replaced at no charge; announces coverage beyond its standard one-year warranty, or regardless of accidental damage, under which cracked or failed Duo inner displays or hinges are repaired or replaced at no charge; announces a recall of the Duo; or an Apple executive states such a policy on the record, including on the Nov. 2 earnings call. A regulator's announcement counts only if it states Apple has agreed to such free repairs. A commitment made in the window counts even if it takes effect later or is later narrowed or withdrawn. These do not count: free replacements given case by case under Apple's standard one-year warranty or at store or carrier discretion; statements that Apple is investigating or that cases are rare; edits to troubleshooting guides; software updates; a paid or discounted repair program or a lower paid repair price; a pause or delay in sales without a free-repair commitment. An announcement dated within the window counts if reported by Nov. 12, 2026. If none is reported by Nov. 12, the answer is Yes.

data.claim: Will China's biggest used-phone dealer keep growing fast as new sales fall?
data.resolution_source: ATRenew Inc. unaudited third-quarter 2026 financial results press release, published on ir.atrenew.com and furnished to the SEC on Form 6-K.
data.resolution_rule: YES if the release reports the number of consumer products transacted in the three months to Sept. 30, 2026 at 12.0 million or more, about 10% above the 10.9 million reported for the third quarter of 2025. NO if it reports less than 12.0 million. If the company redefines the measure, use the year-on-year growth it states for it, or that follows from the comparable prior-year figure it gives: YES at 10% or more, NO below. The figure as first published counts; later revisions do not. Revenue, profit and guidance do not count. VOID if ATRenew has not published its third-quarter 2026 results by Nov. 27, 2026, or if the release gives neither the count nor a comparable growth rate.

data.claim: Will Volkswagen's board hold off approving Audi's Georgia factory into December?
data.resolution_source: Volkswagen AG press releases and ad hoc disclosures (volkswagen-group.com), Audi's media centre, and reporting by Reuters, dpa, Bloomberg or Handelsblatt.
data.resolution_rule: Window: 26 October 2026 through 23:59 CET on Monday 30 November 2026. Reports published by 23:59 CET on Thursday 3 December 2026 count; the question is checked then. NO if any named source reports by then that the supervisory board of Volkswagen AG approved the investment in Audi's planned plant in Georgia (near Macon) within the window, whether at a meeting or by written resolution, alone or as part of the planning round, and even if conditions such as guarantees for German sites are attached; such an approval counts even if later withdrawn, paused or cancelled. YES otherwise, including when nothing at all is reported and when approval comes only on or after 1 December 2026. These do not count as approval: approval by Audi AG's own supervisory board; board decisions that only authorise further planning, site or incentive negotiations, or land options; managers saying approval is expected; the plan being paused, shelved or cancelled before any approval. If a report says the board approved the planning round within the window without saying whether the Georgia plant was included, it counts as approval only if Volkswagen, Audi or one of the named outlets states by the check time that the plant was approved.

data.claim: Will home loans get cheaper while the Fed weighs another rate rise?
data.resolution_source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (freddiemac.com/pmms), weekly release of Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, 30-year fixed-rate average
data.resolution_rule: Yes if the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average in Freddie Mac's release for the survey week of Oct. 29-Nov. 4, 2026, due Nov. 5, is below 7.32%, the figure Freddie Mac published on Oct. 22, 2026 (the last reading before the Oct. 23 bond rally). No if it is 7.32% or higher. The figure as first published counts; later revisions do not. Only that release counts; the Oct. 29 reading does not. If Freddie Mac moves that release to an earlier day, the moved release counts. If no reading for that week is published by Nov. 5, 2026, the question is void.

data.claim: Will Egypt put its economic plan to public debate within a month?
data.resolution_source: Statements by the Egyptian Cabinet (cabinet.gov.eg and its official spokesperson) or Egypt's planning ministry, or reports by Ahram Online, Al-Masry Al-Youm or Egypt's State Information Service
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, between 25 October and 21 November 2026 (Cairo time), the draft 2027-2030 national economic transformation programme or its targets is open to public or societal dialogue, as announced by the Cabinet, its spokesperson or the planning ministry, or reported by one of the named outlets, by 24 November 2026. Either of these counts: the draft or its targets posted for public comment on an official website or app, or at least one session held that is officially presented as part of the dialogue on this programme. A dialogue that opened on 24 October counts if it is reported as open or holding sessions within the window. An opening within the window counts even if the dialogue is later suspended or ended. These do not count: sessions of the Egypt Forum itself (19-24 October), statements that a dialogue will be held, and sessions of the separate National Dialogue on other subjects. No if no such opening within the window is announced or reported by 24 November 2026, including if the dialogue opens only after 21 November or the government skips the dialogue and issues the programme directly.

data.claim: Will Apple keep fixing cracked Duos one by one through Black Friday?
data.resolution_source: Apple's Service Programs page (support.apple.com/service-programs), Apple Newsroom, the transcript of Apple's Nov. 2, 2026 fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call, and on-record Apple statements reported by Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, The Wall Street Journal or CNBC.
data.resolution_rule: Window: the cutoff through 23:59 US Pacific time on Nov. 27, 2026. Resolves NO if, within the window and in any market, either (a) Apple publicly announces a remedy for iPhone Duo inner-screen or hinge failures covering all owners or a defined group of units (such as a serial-number range): a service program, an extended warranty, free repair or replacement beyond normal warranty and AppleCare+ terms, a free part or accessory as a fix, a recall, or a halt to sales over these failures, including a recall or halt ordered by a regulator; or (b) Apple, on record or through a named executive, including on the Nov. 2 earnings call, attributes Duo inner-screen or hinge failures to a common design, component or manufacturing cause, even if it says few units are affected. A remedy or statement later withdrawn still counts. Resolves YES otherwise, including if Apple stays silent, calls the failures rare, isolated or user damage, says it is investigating, publishes folding or care guidance, or keeps repairing or replacing individual phones under warranty or AppleCare+. Only events in the window published or reported by the sources by Nov. 30, 2026 count; silence by then is YES. Unnamed-source reports and leaked internal documents count only if Apple confirms them within the window.

data.claim: Will Cyber Monday computer deals shrink sharply from last year?
data.resolution_source: Adobe Analytics (Adobe Digital Insights) Cyber Monday 2026 results release on news.adobe.com
data.resolution_rule: Yes if Adobe's first results release for Cyber Monday 2026 (Nov. 30, 2026), published by Dec. 6, 2026, reports that discounts on computers peaked at 20% or less off listed price on Cyber Monday. For comparison, Adobe reported 23% for Cyber Monday 2025 and 21.5% for 2024. No if that figure is above 20%. Use the figure exactly as Adobe states it, without rounding. Only the realised Cyber Monday peak counts: ignore forecasts, figures for later days or weeks (such as discounts expected through early December) and figures from releases on Black Friday or earlier days. If the release gives a computers peak only for Cyber Week or Cyber 5 (Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday) rather than Cyber Monday alone, use that figure. If no Adobe release published by Dec. 6, 2026 gives a Cyber Monday, Cyber Week or Cyber 5 peak discount figure for computers, the question is void.

data.claim: Will India raise fertiliser subsidies for the winter crop?
data.resolution_source: Press Information Bureau (pib.gov.in) or pmindia.gov.in release on the Union Cabinet's approval of Nutrient Based Subsidy rates on phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for Rabi 2026-27 (Oct. 1, 2026 to Mar. 31, 2027), together with any Department of Fertilisers or Cabinet release on a special DAP package for that season.
data.resolution_rule: Settle on government approvals made on or before Dec. 4, 2026 and published in the source by Dec. 6, 2026. YES if the phosphorus (P) rate in the first approval of Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates is above Rs 52.76 per kg, the Kharif 2026 rate, or if the Cabinet or Department of Fertilisers approves a new or larger per-tonne special payment on DAP than applied in Kharif 2026, for Rabi 2026-27 sales on top of the NBS rates. NO otherwise, including when the P rate is Rs 52.76 per kg or lower, when Kharif 2026 rates are extended unchanged, or when no Rabi 2026-27 NBS rates and no such DAP payment have been approved and published by Dec. 6, 2026. Statements, media reports or proposals without an approval do not count, and later revisions of the P rate do not change the result of the first approval. Changes to the nitrogen, potash or sulphur rates alone, or to the season's total budget figure alone, do not count.

data.claim: Will America extend its tariff breaks on some Chinese goods?
data.resolution_source: Office of the US Trade Representative press releases and notices (ustr.gov) and the Federal Register
data.resolution_rule: Yes if, by 13 November 2026, USTR (by notice or press release) or the President (by executive order or proclamation) issues a final action extending at least 150 of the 178 Section 301 product exclusions for goods from China (HTSUS headings 9903.88.69 and 9903.88.70), now set to expire on 10 November 2026, to an end date of 9 January 2027 or later, or with no end date. An action issued after the exclusions lapse that applies retroactively counts. Goods on which the Section 301 tariff itself is removed until at least 9 January 2027 count as extended. Proposals, requests for comment and statements of intent by any official do not count, nor does an action withdrawn or shortened below these terms by 13 November. An action issued by 13 November counts if ustr.gov or the Federal Register publishes it by 16 November 2026. No otherwise, including if nothing qualifying is published by 16 November 2026. Void if, by 13 November, the Section 301 tariffs on all 178 excluded goods are removed, so the exclusions no longer matter.
